claim: Extracellular vesicles (EVs) are mediators of cell-cell communication that transport specific protein and RNA cargoes.
source: Extracellular vesicles (EVs) are mediators of cell-cell communication that transport specific protein and RNA cargoes.
evidence: This is a statement of established scientific knowledge about EVs and their function in cell-cell communication.

claim: Exosomes are 30–150 nm in diameter and are released into cell supernatants via fusion of multivesicular bodies (MVBs) with the plasma membrane.
source: Exosomes are 30–150 nm in diameter and are released into cell supernatants via fusion of multivesicular bodies (MVBs) with the plasma membrane.
evidence: This is established scientific knowledge about exosome characteristics and biogenesis.

claim: Full-length Sas (SasFL) has an extracellular domain (ECD) containing a signal peptide, a unique N-terminal region, four von Willebrand factor C (VWFC) domains, and three Fibronectin Type III (FN-III) repeats.
source: Full-length Sas (SasFL) has an extracellular domain (ECD) containing a signal peptide, a unique N-terminal region, four von Willebrand factor C (VWFC) domains, and three Fibronectin Type III (FN-III) repeats (Figure 1a).
evidence: The protein domain structure is described in the text and illustrated in Figure 1a.

claim: The Sasshort isoform lacks a 345 amino acid region of the ECD.
source: A shorter isoform, Sasshort, which is translated from an alternatively spliced mRNA, lacks a 345 amino acid (aa) region of the ECD.
evidence: This is a direct statement about the structural difference between Sas isoforms.

claim: V5-SasFL moves away from expressing cells when expressed in Apterous neurons.
source: SasFL moves away from expressing cells. V5-SasFL was expressed together with mCD8-GFP (transmembrane CSP) in Apterous neurons in late stage 16 embryos.
evidence: Figure 1b shows V5-SasFL localization in areas distant from cell bodies, including sheaths and extracellular regions.

claim: V5-Sasshort is retained in expressing cells and does not move away like V5-SasFL.
source: We also expressed V5-Sasshort in Ap neurons, and observed that V5 staining was restricted to cell bodies and axons in the VNC, and to cell bodies in the brain (Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The localization pattern of V5-Sasshort differs from V5-SasFL, being restricted to expressing cells.

claim: About 50% of V5-SasFL localizes to EVs when expressed in S2 cells.
source: We found that about 50% of V5-SasFL localized to EVs, while ~90% of V5-Sasshort was retained in the cell lysate (Figure 1c).
evidence: Western blot analysis in Figure 1c shows the distribution of SasFL between cell lysate and EV fractions.

claim: About 90% of V5-Sasshort is retained in the cell lysate when expressed in S2 cells.
source: We found that about 50% of V5-SasFL localized to EVs, while ~90% of V5-Sasshort was retained in the cell lysate (Figure 1c).
evidence: Western blot analysis in Figure 1c shows the distribution of Sasshort between cell lysate and EV fractions.

claim: No proteolytic cleavage products of Sas were observed in EVs or unpurified supernatants.
source: We did not observe any proteolytic cleavage products in EVs or unpurified supernatants.
evidence: This is a direct observation from western blot analysis.

claim: SasFL localizes to apical cell surfaces in the foregut and hindgut.
source: Note that in both gut regions SasFL colocalizes with Crumbs at the apical (luminal) cell surfaces (arrows), while anti-Sasshort labels the entire width of the gut wall (brackets).
evidence: Figure 1d shows colocalization of SasFL with the apical marker Crumbs.

claim: Sasshort is distributed across the entire cell membrane in the foregut and hindgut.
source: Note that in both gut regions SasFL colocalizes with Crumbs at the apical (luminal) cell surfaces (arrows), while anti-Sasshort labels the entire width of the gut wall (brackets).
evidence: Figure 1d shows Sasshort distribution across the entire gut wall.

claim: The EVT sequence lacking in Sasshort is required for both apical localization and targeting to EVs.
source: These data imply that the EVT sequence lacking in Sasshort is required for both apical localization and targeting to EVs.
evidence: This is inferred from the differential localization patterns of SasFL and Sasshort.

claim: EVs from V5-SasFL-expressing S2 cells span a range of sizes from ~30 nm to >100 nm in diameter.
source: The tomographic images showed that the EVs span a range of sizes, from ~30 nm in diameter to >100 nm, and that they are a mixture of single and double-membrane vesicles (Figure 2c and d, Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: EM tomography images show the size distribution of EVs.

claim: EVs from V5-SasFL-expressing S2 cells are a mixture of single and double-membrane vesicles.
source: The tomographic images showed that the EVs span a range of sizes, from ~30 nm in diameter to >100 nm, and that they are a mixture of single and double-membrane vesicles (Figure 2c and d, Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: EM tomography images show both single and double-membrane vesicles.

claim: The distance between the EV membrane and gold particles in immuno-EM can be more than 40 nm.
source: The distance between the EV membrane (yellow bracket: diameter of the vesicle) and a gold particle (white bracket: distance between membrane and a particle) can be more than 40 nm.
evidence: Figure 2a shows measurements of distances between EV membrane and gold particles.

claim: The large distance between the EV membrane and gold particles likely reflects the large size of the Sas ECD.
source: This likely reflects the large size of the Sas ECD, in which the N-terminal V5 epitope is separated by 1590 aa from the TM domain.
evidence: This is an inference based on the protein structure and the observed distances in immuno-EM.

claim: Expression of SasFL increased the number of EVs per cell in the exosome size range (30–150 nm in diameter) by 44%.
source: Expression of SasFL increased the number of EVs per cell in the exosome size range (30–150 nm in diameter) by 44%, and the number of EVs per cell of <100 nm in diameter by 72%, suggesting that the presence of high levels of SasFL increases the rate of EV production.
evidence: NTA analysis in Figure 2e shows increased EV production in SasFL-expressing cells.

claim: Expression of SasFL increased the number of EVs per cell of <100 nm in diameter by 72%.
source: Expression of SasFL increased the number of EVs per cell in the exosome size range (30–150 nm in diameter) by 44%, and the number of EVs per cell of <100 nm in diameter by 72%, suggesting that the presence of high levels of SasFL increases the rate of EV production.
evidence: NTA analysis in Figure 2e shows increased EV production in SasFL-expressing cells.

claim: The distribution of EV diameters was shifted toward smaller values in cells expressing SasFL (mean diameter = 102 nm, vs. 129 nm for control cells).
source: We observed that the distribution of EV diameters was shifted toward smaller values in cells expressing SasFL (mean diameter = 102 nm, vs. 129 nm for control cells) (Figure 2e).
evidence: NTA analysis in Figure 2e shows the size distribution of EVs.

claim: Many EVs from V5-SasFL-expressing S2 cells had denser objects within their boundaries, typically 30–40 nm in diameter.
source: Many of the EVs from V5-SasFL-expressing S2 cells EVs had denser objects within their boundaries (Figure 2d, Figure 2—figure supplement 1). These were typically 30–40 nm in diameter.
evidence: EM tomography images show denser objects within EVs.

claim: V5-SasFL made in salivary glands is present in imaginal discs, which are separated from SGs by larval hemolymph.
source: We found that V5-SasFL made in SGs is present in imaginal discs, which are separated from SGs by larval hemolymph (wing and haltere discs shown in Figure 3a–c).
evidence: Figure 3b shows V5 staining in imaginal discs when SasFL is expressed in salivary glands.

claim: V5-Sasshort expressed in salivary glands is not observed in imaginal discs.
source: We also expressed V5-Sasshort in SGs, and this was not observed in imaginal discs (Figure 3c).
evidence: Figure 3c shows absence of V5 staining in imaginal discs when Sasshort is expressed in salivary glands.

claim: Expression of Ptp10D in recipient S2 cells increased V5-SasFL levels in these cells.
source: We observed that expression of the Sas receptor Ptp10D in recipient cells increased V5-SasFL levels in these cells, as did expression of Numb, a regulator of endocytosis that binds to the Sas ICD (Chien et al., 1998).
evidence: Western blot analysis in Figure 3g shows increased V5-SasFL in cells expressing Ptp10D.

claim: Expression of Numb in recipient S2 cells increased V5-SasFL levels in these cells.
source: We observed that expression of the Sas receptor Ptp10D in recipient cells increased V5-SasFL levels in these cells, as did expression of Numb, a regulator of endocytosis that binds to the Sas ICD (Chien et al., 1998).
evidence: Western blot analysis in Figure 3g shows increased V5-SasFL in cells expressing Numb.

claim: Expression of both Ptp10D and Numb produced a synergistic effect, increasing V5-SasFL by ~fourfold relative to untransfected recipient cells.
source: Expression of both Ptp10D and Numb produced a synergistic effect, increasing V5-SasFL by ~fourfold relative to untransfected recipient cells (Figure 3g–h).
evidence: Western blot and quantification in Figures 3g-h show synergistic effect of Ptp10D and Numb coexpression.

claim: Ptp10D is a binding partner for Sas.
source: In earlier work, we identified the receptor tyrosine phosphatase (RPTP) Ptp10D as a binding partner for Sas, and showed that Sas::Ptp10D interactions regulate embryonic axon guidance, as well as glial migration and proliferation (Lee et al., 2013).
evidence: This is cited from previous work by the authors.

claim: Sas::Ptp10D interactions regulate embryonic axon guidance, as well as glial migration and proliferation.
source: In earlier work, we identified the receptor tyrosine phosphatase (RPTP) Ptp10D as a binding partner for Sas, and showed that Sas::Ptp10D interactions regulate embryonic axon guidance, as well as glial migration and proliferation (Lee et al., 2013).
evidence: This is cited from previous work by the authors.

claim: dArc1 was the most highly enriched protein (after Sas itself) in mass spectrometry analysis of V5-SasFL EVs, with 22-fold enrichment.
source: We observed that the most highly enriched protein (after Sas itself) is dArc1 (22-fold) (Figure 4b).
evidence: Mass spectrometry data in Figure 4b shows dArc1 enrichment in V5-SasFL EVs.

claim: dArc2 is enriched 6-fold in V5-SasFL EVs compared to control EVs.
source: dArc2 is #7 on the list (6-fold).
evidence: Mass spectrometry data in Figure 4b shows dArc2 enrichment in V5-SasFL EVs.

claim: dArc1 mRNA is a prominent mRNA component of EVs from Drosophila cultured cells.
source: dArc1 mRNA, presumably encapsulated within dArc1 capsids, is known to be a prominent mRNA component of EVs from Drosophila cultured cells (Lefebvre et al., 2016; Ashley et al., 2018).
evidence: This is cited from previous published work.

claim: dArc1 binds directly to the Sas ICD.
source: We then went on to show that dArc1 binds directly to the Sas ICD (see below).
evidence: This is demonstrated through co-IP and peptide binding assays shown in Figure 4.

claim: dArc1 co-IP'd with the Sas ICD fusion protein in S2 cells.
source: We observed that dArc1 co-IP'd with the Sas ICD fusion protein (Figure 4c).
evidence: Co-IP experiment in Figure 4c shows interaction between dArc1 and Sas ICD.

claim: The Sas ICD sequence contains the sequence motif YDNPSY.
source: The Sas ICD sequence contains the sequence motif YDNPSY, which is a PTB-binding motif (NPXY) that overlaps by two amino acids with an SH2-binding motif (YXXP) that is also a potential Abl tyrosine kinase substrate sequence (Colicelli, 2010; Figure 4e).
evidence: The sequence is shown in Figure 4e and described in the text.

claim: The NPXY motif in Sas is the target for binding of the Numb PTB.
source: The NPXY motif is the target for binding of the Numb PTB (Li et al., 1998).
evidence: This is cited from previous published work.

claim: Appl contains the sequence YENPTY in its ICD.
source: We searched for other Drosophila CSPs containing a sequence with similar properties in their ICDs, and found only one, Appl, which has the sequence YENPTY but is otherwise unrelated to the Sas ICD.
evidence: The sequence is shown in Figure 4e and described in the text.

claim: Human APP contains the sequence YENPTY in its ICD.
source: Human APP, the mammalian ortholog of Appl, contains the same sequence in its short ICD (Figure 4e), as do the two APP paralogs, APLP1 and APLP2.
evidence: The sequence is shown in Figure 4e and described in the text.

claim: The Appl ICD protein co-IP'd with dArc1-Myc.
source: We then replaced the Sas ICD in the V5-mCD8ECD-SasTM-ICD construct with the Appl and APP ICDs, and found that the Appl ICD protein co-IP'd with dArc1-Myc (Figure 4c), implicating the Y(D/E)NP(S/T)Y sequence in binding to dArc1.
evidence: Co-IP experiment in Figure 4c shows interaction between dArc1 and Appl ICD.

claim: Myc-rArcFL was able to co-IP with the Sas and APP ICDs.
source: We observed that Myc-rArcFL was able to co-IP with the Sas and APP ICDs (Figure 4c).
evidence: Co-IP experiment in Figure 4c shows interaction between mammalian Arc and Sas/APP ICDs.

claim: GST-dArc1 bound to the wild-type Sas ICD peptide but not to scrambled or YDNPSY deletion mutant Sas peptides.
source: In the peptide binding assay, we observed that dArc1 directly bound to the Sas ICD peptide, but not to the other peptides.
evidence: Peptide binding assay in Figure 4d shows specific binding of dArc1 to wild-type Sas ICD peptide.

claim: GST-rArcFL bound to the Sas ICD peptide and the APP ICD peptide.
source: Mammalian Arc also bound to the Sas ICD peptide, as well as to the APP ICD peptide (Figure 4d).
evidence: Peptide binding assay in Figure 4d shows binding of mammalian Arc to Sas and APP ICD peptides.

claim: Mammalian and Drosophila Arc are not orthologs and are apparently derived from independent Ty3/gypsy retrotransposon lineages.
source: Mammalian and Drosophila Arc are not orthologs, and are apparently derived from independent Ty3/gypsy retrotransposon lineages (Ashley et al., 2018; Pastuzyn et al., 2018; Hantak et al., 2021).
evidence: This is cited from previous published work.

claim: The Y(D/E)NP(S/T)Y sequence is a determinant of binding to Arcs.
source: Our results implicate the Y(D/E)NP(S/T)Y sequence as a determinant of binding to Arcs (Figure 4e), and show that fly and mammalian Arcs can bind to the same peptide sequences.
evidence: This is inferred from the co-IP and peptide binding experiments showing that proteins with this motif bind to Arc proteins.

claim: APP localizes to EVs.
source: APP also localizes to EVs (Laulagnier et al., 2018; Pérez-González et al., 2020).
evidence: This is cited from previous published work.

claim: Arc has been implicated in Alzheimer's disease pathogenesis.
source: The connection between APP and Arc will be of interest to explore in future studies, since Arc has been implicated in AD pathogenesis (Wu et al., 2011; Landgren et al., 2012; Bi et al., 2018).
evidence: This is cited from previous published work.

claim: V5-SasFL expressed in salivary glands moves to the gut and tracheae in late stage 16 embryos.
source: To establish an assay system for dArc1 capsid movement in embryos, we first expressed V5-SasFL in late stage 16 embryonic SGs together with RFP, and observed that V5 signal moved to the gut and tracheae, while RFP was retained in the SGs as expected.
evidence: This is shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1.

claim: V5-Sasshort expressed in salivary glands is only observed in the SGs and not in other tissues.
source: When V5-Sasshort was expressed in SGs, however, V5 staining was only observed in the SGs (Figure 5—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1.

claim: dArc1 is made at very low levels in embryos.
source: dArc1 is made at very low levels in embryos.
evidence: This is a direct observation from antibody staining experiments.

claim: When SasFL and dArc1 were expressed together in salivary glands, there were many bright puncta stained with anti-dArc1 in the dorsal tracheal trunk.
source: Figure 5d' shows that, in late stage 16 embryos expressing both SasFL and dArc1 in SGs, there were many bright puncta stained with anti-dArc1 in the dorsal tracheal trunk, which expresses Ptp10D.
evidence: Figure 5d' shows dArc1 puncta in tracheal trunk when SasFL and dArc1 are coexpressed.

claim: No dArc1 puncta were detectable in control embryos (Sage-GAL4/+) in the dorsal tracheal trunk.
source: They were not detectable in control embryos (Sage-GAL4/+; Figure 5a').
evidence: Figure 5a' shows absence of dArc1 puncta in control embryos.

claim: Exogenous dArc1 induces expression of endogenous dArc1 mRNA.
source: This shows that exogenous dArc1 induces expression of endogenous dArc1 mRNA (or stabilizes the mRNA).
evidence: FISH analysis shows increased endogenous dArc1 mRNA signal when exogenous dArc1 is expressed.

claim: When SasFL and dArc1 were expressed together in salivary glands, the entire tracheal system is lit up by the FISH signal for the endogenous dArc1 3' UTR.
source: Finally, when SasFL and dArc1 were expressed together, we observed a completely different pattern, in which the entire tracheal system is lit up by the FISH signal for the endogenous dArc1 3' UTR (Figure 5h).
evidence: Figure 5h shows bright FISH signal throughout the tracheal system.

claim: dArc1 mRNA lacking the endogenous dArc1 3' UTR sequences is not efficiently loaded into dArc1 capsids that can move elsewhere in the embryo.
source: This suggests that dArc1 mRNA lacking the endogenous dArc1 3' UTR sequences is not efficiently loaded into dArc1 capsids that can move elsewhere in the embryo.
evidence: FISH with SV40 3' UTR probe shows signal only in SGs, not in distant tissues.

claim: The dArc1 3' UTR is required for dArc1 mRNA transfer at the NMJ.
source: This is consistent with the findings of Ashley et al., 2018, who showed that the dArc1 3' UTR is required for dArc1 mRNA transfer at the NMJ.
evidence: This is cited from previous published work.

claim: The Sas ICD is required for dArc1 mRNA transport to tracheal cells.
source: Finally, we examined whether the Sas ICD is required for dArc1 mRNA transport by expressing dArc1 together with a protein (SasECD-TM-GFP) in which the Sas ICD was replaced by GFP. This protein is present in EVs when expressed in S2 cells, but it does not produce any dArc1 FISH signal outside of the SGs (Figure 5—figure supplement 2), indicating that it cannot facilitate transport of dArc1 capsids to tracheal cells.
evidence: Figure 5—figure supplement 2 shows absence of dArc1 FISH signal outside SGs when Sas ICD is replaced by GFP.

claim: SasFL is an EV targeting ligand that can direct internalization of EVs into cells expressing the Sas receptor Ptp10D.
source: These findings contribute to the understanding of intercellular communication mechanisms by showing that SasFL is an EV targeting ligand that can direct internalization of EVs into cells expressing the Sas receptor Ptp10D.
evidence: This is a summary conclusion based on the experimental data showing preferential targeting of SasFL EVs to Ptp10D-expressing cells.

claim: Endogenous SasFL is likely to move between cells in vivo.
source: Endogenous SasFL is likely to move between cells in vivo, because tagged SasFL moves away from both neuronal and non-neuronal cells when ectopically expressed.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that tagged SasFL moves away from expressing cells.

claim: dArc1 forms a capsid that contains dArc1 mRNA and is loaded into EVs.
source: dArc1 is related to retrotransposon Gag proteins, and it forms a capsid that contains dArc1 mRNA and is loaded into EVs (Ashley et al., 2018).
evidence: This is cited from previous published work.

claim: Overexpressed SasFL can facilitate transfer of dArc1 capsids into distant Ptp10D-expressing recipient cells in vivo.
source: Overexpressed SasFL can facilitate transfer of dArc1 capsids into distant Ptp10D-expressing recipient cells in vivo.
evidence: This is demonstrated by the FISH and immunostaining experiments showing dArc1 and dArc1 mRNA in tracheal cells when SasFL and dArc1 are coexpressed in SGs.

claim: Mammalian Arc forms capsids that are transported via EVs.
source: Mammalian Arc also forms capsids that are transported via EVs (Pastuzyn et al., 2018), and it binds to the Sas and APP ICDs, which share a tyrosine motif.
evidence: This is cited from previous published work.

claim: Full-length APP and some of its proteolytic products are localized to EVs.
source: Full-length APP and some of its proteolytic products are localized to EVs, and EVs from N2a cells bearing tagged APP are internalized into cultured neurons, but not into glia (Laulagnier et al., 2018).
evidence: This is cited from previous published work.

claim: EVs from N2a cells bearing tagged APP are internalized into cultured neurons, but not into glia.
source: Full-length APP and some of its proteolytic products are localized to EVs, and EVs from N2a cells bearing tagged APP are internalized into cultured neurons, but not into glia (Laulagnier et al., 2018).
evidence: This is cited from previous published work.

claim: sas mutant larvae die at or before second instar and have tracheal phenotypes in larvae but no known phenotypes in embryos.
source: sas mutant larvae die at or before second instar (hence the name stranded at second, which is derived from baseball terminology) and have tracheal phenotypes in larvae but no known phenotypes in embryos (Schonbaum et al., 1992).
evidence: This is cited from previous published work.

claim: A tyrosine motif in the Sas ICD was found to bind to the PTB domain of Numb.
source: A tyrosine motif in the Sas ICD was found to bind to the PTB domain of Numb (Chien et al., 1998), an protein involved in endocytosis that is a negative regulator of Notch signaling.
evidence: This is cited from previous published work.

claim: Mammalian Arc is a locally translated dendritic protein that regulates synaptic plasticity, in part by modulating endocytosis of AMPA receptors.
source: Mammalian Arc is a locally translated dendritic protein that regulates synaptic plasticity, in part by modulating endocytosis of AMPA receptors (Chowdhury et al., 2006; Shepherd et al., 2006).
evidence: This is cited from previous published work.

claim: The Drosophila genome encodes two proteins distantly related to mammalian Arc, dArc1 and dArc2.
source: The Drosophila genome encodes two proteins distantly related to mammalian Arc, dArc1 and dArc2.
evidence: This is established knowledge about the Drosophila genome.

claim: dArc1 functions in larval and adult brain neurons to regulate aspects of metabolism.
source: dArc1 functions in larval and adult brain neurons to regulate aspects of metabolism (Mattaliano et al., 2007; Mosher et al., 2015; Keith et al., 2021).
evidence: This is cited from previous published work.

claim: Arc and dArc1 evolved independently from retrotransposon Gag proteins.
source: Arc and dArc1 evolved independently from retrotransposon Gag proteins (Shepherd, 2018).
evidence: This is cited from previous published work.

claim: Arc and dArc1 both form virus-like capsids that can encapsulate Arc mRNAs and are transported between cells via EVs.
source: Remarkably, they both form virus-like capsids that can encapsulate Arc mRNAs and are transported between cells via EVs (Ashley et al., 2018; Pastuzyn et al., 2018; Hantak et al., 2021).
evidence: This is cited from previous published work.

claim: dArc1 has a C-terminal Zn2+ finger that might be involved in nucleic acid binding.
source: dArc1, but not dArc2, has a C-terminal Zn2+ finger that might be involved in nucleic acid binding (Pastuzyn et al., 2018; Erlendsson et al., 2020).
evidence: This is cited from previous published work.

claim: RNA is required for normal mammalian Arc capsid assembly.
source: Mammalian Arc lacks Zn2+ fingers, but RNA is required for normal capsid assembly (Pastuzyn et al., 2018).
evidence: This is cited from previous published work.

claim: Drosophila dArc1 capsids bearing dArc1 mRNA move from neurons to muscles across larval neuromuscular junction (NMJ) synapses.
source: Drosophila dArc1 capsids bearing dArc1 mRNA move from neurons to muscles across larval neuromuscular junction (NMJ) synapses, and dArc1 transfer is required for activity-induced induction of morphological synaptic plasticity (Ashley et al., 2018).
evidence: This is cited from previous published work.

claim: dArc1 transfer is required for activity-induced induction of morphological synaptic plasticity at the NMJ.
source: Drosophila dArc1 capsids bearing dArc1 mRNA move from neurons to muscles across larval neuromuscular junction (NMJ) synapses, and dArc1 transfer is required for activity-induced induction of morphological synaptic plasticity (Ashley et al., 2018).
evidence: This is cited from previous published work.

claim: Sas-bearing EVs preferentially target to cells expressing Ptp10D.
source: Sas is a binding partner for the Ptp10D receptor tyrosine phosphatase, and Sas-bearing EVs preferentially target to cells expressing Ptp10D.
evidence: This is demonstrated by the experiments showing increased uptake of SasFL EVs by Ptp10D-expressing cells.

claim: The cytoplasmic domain (ICD) of Sas binds to dArc1 and mammalian Arc.
source: We used co-immunoprecipitation and peptide binding to show that the cytoplasmic domain (ICD) of Sas binds to dArc1 and mammalian Arc.
evidence: This is demonstrated by co-IP and peptide binding experiments in Figure 4.

claim: The Sas ICD contains a motif required for dArc1 binding that is shared by the mammalian and Drosophila amyloid precursor protein (APP) orthologs.
source: The Sas ICD contains a motif required for dArc1 binding that is shared by the mammalian and Drosophila amyloid precursor protein (APP) orthologs, and the APP ICD also binds to mammalian Arc.
evidence: This is demonstrated by the sequence analysis and binding experiments showing that Sas, APP, and Appl ICDs share the Y(D/E)NP(S/T)Y motif and bind to Arc proteins.

claim: The APP ICD binds to mammalian Arc.
source: The Sas ICD contains a motif required for dArc1 binding that is shared by the mammalian and Drosophila amyloid precursor protein (APP) orthologs, and the APP ICD also binds to mammalian Arc.
evidence: This is demonstrated by co-IP and peptide binding experiments in Figure 4.

claim: Sas facilitates delivery of dArc1 capsids bearing dArc1 mRNA into distant Ptp10D-expressing recipient cells in vivo.
source: Sas facilitates delivery of dArc1 capsids bearing dArc1 mRNA into distant Ptp10D-expressing recipient cells in vivo.
evidence: This is demonstrated by the FISH and immunostaining experiments showing dArc1 and dArc1 mRNA in tracheal cells when SasFL and dArc1 are coexpressed in SGs.

claim: EVs contain the Wg protein, which is a marker for EVs in S2 cells.
source: EVs contained the Wg protein, which is a marker for EVs in S2 cells and is present at very low levels in lysates (Koles et al., 2012; Figure 1c, Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: Western blot in Figure 1c shows Wg in EV fractions, and this is cited from previous work.

claim: EVs lack β-actin, showing that they are not heavily contaminated by cytosol.
source: They lacked β-actin, showing that they are not heavily contaminated by cytosol.
evidence: Western blot in Figure 1c shows absence of β-actin in EV fractions.

claim: EV preparations made using the Exosome Isolation kit have similar characteristics to those generated by ultracentrifugation.
source: EV preparations made using the Exosome Isolation kit have similar characteristics to those generated by ultracentrifugation (Skottvoll et al., 2019), and the kit requires much less material, allowing EVs to be purified from small-scale transfections.
evidence: This is cited from previous published work.

claim: The dArc1 capsid is 37 nm in diameter.
source: The dArc1 capsid is 37 nm in diameter (Erlendsson et al., 2020; Hallin et al., 2021).
evidence: This is cited from previous published work.

claim: EVs from media of short-term cultures of mouse cortical neurons contain denser objects whose size (~30 nm in diameter) is consistent with mammalian Arc capsids.
source: EVs from media of short-term cultures of mouse cortical neurons were shown to contain denser objects whose size (~30 nm in diameter) was consistent with mammalian Arc capsids, and which were associated with anti-Arc gold particles (Pastuzyn et al., 2018).
evidence: This is cited from previous published work.

claim: Capsid-like structures that bound to anti-dArc1 gold particles were detected in lysed preparations of EVs from S2 cells.
source: For dArc1, capsid-like structures that bound to anti-dArc1 gold particles were detected in lysed preparations of EVs from S2 cells (Ashley et al., 2018).
evidence: This is cited from previous published work.

claim: The Y(D/E)NP(S/T)Y sequence contains the consensus motif for binding of mammalian Arc to TARPγ2, CaMKII, and NMDA receptor peptides, which is X-P-X-(Y/F/H).
source: This sequence contains the consensus motif for binding of mammalian Arc to TARPγ2, CaMKII, and NMDA receptor peptides, which is X-P-X-(Y/F/H)(Zhang et al., 2015; Nielsen et al., 2019).
evidence: This is cited from previous published work.

claim: Arc binds to the NMDA receptor as a monomer.
source: Arc binds to the NMDA receptor as a monomer (Nielsen et al., 2019).
evidence: This is cited from previous published work.

claim: The first Y in the YENPTY motif in APP has been reported to be a substrate for the Abl tyrosine kinase.
source: The first Y in the YENPTY motif in APP has been reported to be a substrate for the Abl tyrosine kinase (Zambrano et al., 2001).
evidence: This is cited from previous published work.

claim: The Abl inhibitor imatinib (Gleevec) inhibits formation of β-amyloid peptide (Aβ).
source: The Abl inhibitor imatinib (Gleevec), which would be expected to block phosphorylation of this site, inhibits formation of β-amyloid peptide (Aβ)(Netzer et al., 2003), and binding of Arc to APP could be relevant to this effect.
evidence: This is cited from previous published work.

claim: Binding of Numb to the Sas ICD may increase Sas uptake and/or protect endocytosed Sas from degradation.
source: We speculate that binding of Numb to the Sas ICD increases Sas uptake and/or protects endocytosed Sas from degradation.
evidence: This is speculation based on the observed synergistic effect of Numb and Ptp10D on SasFL uptake.

claim: Sas is not required for loading of dArc1 capsids into EVs.
source: Sas is not required for loading of dArc1 capsids into EVs, since dArc1 mRNA is a normal component of EVs from cell lines that do not express Sas.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that dArc1 mRNA is found in EVs from cells that don't express Sas.

claim: Binding of Sas to dArc1 may help to increase the probability that Sas-bearing EVs contain dArc1 capsids bearing dArc1 mRNA.
source: Binding of Sas to dArc1 may help to increase the probability that Sas-bearing EVs contain dArc1 capsids bearing dArc1 mRNA.
evidence: This is speculation about the functional role of Sas-dArc1 interaction.

claim: One function of Sas might be to deliver EVs and their dArc1 capsid cargo, including encapsulated RNA, to specific recipient cells that express the Sas binding partner Ptp10D.
source: One function of Sas might then be to deliver the EVs and their dArc1 capsid cargo, including encapsulated RNA, to specific recipient cells that express the Sas binding partner Ptp10D.
evidence: This is speculation about the functional role of Sas in EV targeting.

claim: The brightness of the tracheal FISH signal suggests that it represents not only dArc1 mRNA transferred from capsids, but dArc1 mRNA synthesized in these cells in response to dArc1 protein made from the dArc1 mRNA transported in the capsid.
source: The brightness of the tracheal FISH signal suggests that it represents not only dArc1 mRNA transferred from capsids, but dArc1 mRNA synthesized in these cells in response to dArc1 protein made from the dArc1 mRNA transported in the capsid.
evidence: This is inferred from the intensity of the FISH signal in tracheal cells.

claim: There is a glial sheath around the VNC at late stage 16.
source: There is a glial sheath around the VNC at late stage 16, and this might block access of EVs to Ptp10D-expressing neurons.
evidence: This is stated as a possible explanation for why dArc1 is not observed in VNC neurons.

claim: Sas::Ptp10D interactions control the elimination of neoplastic epithelial clones by surrounding normal tissue.
source: Sas::Ptp10D interactions also control the elimination of neoplastic epithelial clones by surrounding normal tissue. Sas is on normal epithelial cells, and it relocalizes to the parts of their cell surfaces that are adjacent to the neoplastic clone and binds to Ptp10D on the neoplastic cells. Ptp10D in turn relocalizes and dephosphorylates the EGF receptor tyrosine kinase, leading to death of the neoplastic cells (Yamamoto et al., 2017).
evidence: This is cited from previous published work.

claim: The Sas ECD has binding partners other than Ptp10D.
source: The Sas ECD has other binding partners as well, because it interacts with cells that do not express Ptp10D in live embryo staining assays (Lee et al., 2013).
evidence: This is cited from previous published work.
